ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.44 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexempted detour segment; note the driver's RD-1 breach (deviating to a station he never used) on the record.

segment_findings.reason: RD-3(b): the rider agreed only to a one-minute stop at a petrol station 'just ahead' [F7][F8] (21:44, before the 21:47 segment start); the driver chose a point 979 m off the optimal route producing 1.76 km driven vs 0.03 km optimal, so the 1.73 km extra is not excused by the stop request. RD-4: no traffic incident near the route [F12], only bands 4/5 on other expressways [F10][F11], and RD-4(b) bands alone do not exempt. RD-5: consent did not cover this route change. extra_km 1.73 × $1.4109/km = $2.44 refundable.

rejected_claims.reason: The $2.90 billed excess covers the full 2.1 km trip excess; only the 1.73 km segment-attributable extra is refundable under RD-2 ($2.44), the ~0.37 km balance being unexplained map-matching/fare residual.
Speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on SIE is not band 1–2 and is not tied to the replaced optimal segment; under RD-4(b) it cannot exempt the detour.
Speed band 5 on TPE is general congestion on another road, not an incident on the substituted optimal segment; RD-4(c) applies.
Rider profile facts cannot decide a case and are irrelevant here.
Driver's upheld disputes are no-show related (route upheld = 0), so RD-6's route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 condition is not met; no account flag.
